items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: I got the chance to perform with him too, with the group... We did a gig with his band.

ctx.x: So is studying the music mostly an oral thing listening to recordings?

It’s both listening, but you have to play. You have to attack it. Because you can listen to it now, transmitted to your hands so you can play it the way you hear it. You know? So © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

now you have to do a lot of listening because there’s a lot of different styles. Latin music, it’s not just Latin music. There’s big band Latin music, there’s cojunto there’s charanga there’s son montuno there’s trio music. So which branch of Latin music that you play now. So now we start to open up the can. What do you want to do? Do you like big band? So I’m going to listen to Machito, I’m going to listen to not even Xavier Cugat, he was kind of a cross bridge between the Latin and the American you know. He was…
